Analysts predict continued strong demand for Chinese tech products, although it may exacerbate domestic economic imbalances. (Source: reuters.com)

4. **[UA regents delay statement of intent on AI amid feedback](https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/11/10/ua-regents-delay-statement-intent-ai-amid-feedback)** - The University of Alaska Board of Regents has postponed a statement regarding the use of AI in its system, allowing time for feedback from faculty and students. (Source: alaskasnewssource.com)

5. **[Congress’s Permitting Bill Is a ‘Massive Giveaway’ to the AI Data Center Industry, Critics Warn](https://time.com/article/2026/11/10/permitting-bill-data-centers)** - Critics argue that a new permitting bill in Congress could disproportionately benefit the AI data center industry, raising concerns about the implications for public input on AI's role in society. (Source: time.com)

items.title: AI and your job: Threat or opportunity?
items.summary:
MOBILE, Ala. (WALA) - Artificial intelligence is becoming a bigger part of everyday life, raising questions about what the technology could mean for workers and their jobs.

Some economists believe AI poses a particular threat to entry-level and repetitive work, including call center, data entry and junior copywriting jobs, according to The Wall Street Journal. Those tasks may be easier to automate. [...] But AI could also create opportunities. A Bloomberg article points to potential job growth in construction and manufacturing as companies build data centers and produce the chips that power the technology. Some higher-skilled office workers could also benefit if AI helps them become more productive. [...] The long-term impact on jobs remains unclear, but workers can take steps to prepare. Exploring AI chatbots, writing assistants and other tools may help people find ways to work more efficiently and develop skills that complement the technology.

items.title: Asia not riding but building the AI boom – GIS Reports
items.summary:
The AI ecosystem can be generally separated between three elements: models, compute power and supply chains – with the U.S. and China competing and leading for the first two. Asian countries are looking at how they can stand out amid this intense East-West competition, while capitalizing on their strengths in technology manufacturing supply chains. This has led smaller economies to identify their competitive advantages while investing in novel applications for AI in various industries such as [...] Due to demographic realities, manufacturing and exports are essential to Asian economies. AI is expected to support transitions as each country manages declines in their populations and workforce while maintaining economic growth and prosperity.

Receive insights from our experts every week in your inbox. [...] AI is now a priority for all governments in Asia, with each taking a different approach. Government-to-government coordination is focusing on finding ways to collaborate in the regulatory space on issues like export controls and supply chain monitoring. Elected officials are looking to support their domestic industries in the hope that local companies increase their participation in global markets.

## The epicenter of AI technology is Taiwan

items.title: China's trade surplus soars past $1 trillion as AI boom powers exports | Reuters
items.summary:
Much of the strength in exports this ​year has been fuelled by a global push to expand AI infrastructure.

"The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last," Macquarie analysts wrote. They expect China's exports to accelerate ​further in the fourth quarter before starting to slow from the first quarter of 2027.

Reporting by Yukun Zhang, Sam Li and Ryan Woo; Editing by Shri Navaratnam

Our Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles. [...] BEIJING, Nov 10 (Reuters) - China's trade surplus surged past $1 trillion in the first 10 months as a global race to build AI infrastructure buoyed sales ​of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic likely to sharpen tensions with major trading partners. [...] The figures highlight ‌Beijing's growing reliance on overseas demand to support an economy hobbled by subdued consumption and a protracted property slump. But while the global AI investment boom is expected to keep demand for Chinese technology products strong into 2027, it risks deepening domestic imbalances and fuelling trade frictions with partners including the European Union.

items.title: UA regents delay statement of intent on AI amid feedback
items.summary:
Work on the university system’s intent language began in 2025, Taylor said, when faculty requested guidance from administration on the use of AI in the classroom.

When complete, the document is designed not to act as policy, but simply to outline the approach the UA institution is taking toward AI, develop guiding principles and put forward expectations of future actions from the administration, including eventually coming up with actual policy. [...] The action was recommended by Chief Technology Officer Benjamin Shier, and pushes off the final decision on the university system’s AI intent language until February, or until requested by UA President Matt Cooper.

Taylor described the feedback being received about the draft “AI Engaged” document as “passionate.” [...] FAIRBANKS, Alaska (KTUU/KTVF) - The University of Alaska (UA) Board of Regents delayed releasing a statement of intent covering the system’s use of artificial intelligence during its November meeting Friday, giving the information technology department time to incorporate feedback from faculty, staff and students into the document.
